comparison_seed.source: Danish EU-residence regulation and official guidance previously used in the EEA/Swiss expansion
comparison_seed.relationship_note: France's CESEDA codifies EU-citizen and family-member provisions inside a broader immigration code. Similar topic and some shared functions do not establish equivalent wording, scope, competent authority, or procedure. EU rules remain in the shared EU core.

previous_findings_carried_forward: The earlier France register contained seven unaccepted candidates focused on CESEDA, civil status, international adoption, France-Visas, and the administrative courts. They were reconciled here and retained as candidates.

The earlier France-Visas HTTP request returned 403 and yielded only a browser-derived summary. The official page rendered in the research browser on 2026-10-18, but that does not create a raw capture or converted source text; the old limitation remains relevant to a future runtime adapter.

The CESEDA EU-family provisions were previously flagged for judicially annulled wording. The Conseil d'État decision of 24 February 2022, no. 450285 (including joined no. 450288), confirms that Articles L. 233-1 and L. 233-2 were annulled in part for a defined category of dependent children of an EU citizen studying or training in France. The decision must be linked to any future article-level monitor.

Czechia's keyless, date-bound PDF route, Estonia's structured XML route, and Finland's documented no-registration API were carried forward as adapter-design precedents only. They do not prove a French endpoint or converter works.

The earlier taxonomy review identified procedure, records access, remedies, consular practice, privacy, oversight, and courts as separate source classes. Each was searched separately here; legal codes alone do not establish coverage of these classes.

N-Lex identifies Légifrance as France's official legal-information site, but N-Lex is used only as a national-law discovery lead and is not a substitute for ministry, court, oversight, or service publishers.
